title: useDeferredValue Simulation with Debounced Low-Priority Clone
problemStatement: Implement `createDeferredValue(initialValue, delayMs = 15)` that receives urgent value updates, but delays updating the returned deferred value to keep rendering responsive.
interviewTrap: `useDeferredValue` is not just a debounce; in true React 18, React begins rendering the deferred value in memory and aborts it immediately if another urgent update arrives.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React categorizes updates into Urgent (typing in an `<input>`, clicks) and Non-Urgent / Transition (filtering a 10,000 item list). Wrapping an update in `startTransition(() => setQuery(text))` allows React to interrupt the list render if the user types another keystroke.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Lagged Rendering via useDeferredValue.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does useDeferredValue differ from useTransition?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `startTransition` wraps the state update function at the trigger site (`startTransition(() => setState())`). `useDeferredValue` wraps a value itself (`const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query)`). It is used when you do not own the `setState` dispatcher (e.g. receiving a value from props or third-party libraries).
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of when to use which concurrency hook.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does useDeferredValue differ from debounce?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Debounce waits for a fixed time delay (e.g. 300ms) before doing any work, introducing an artificial lag even on fast computers. `useDeferredValue` has NO fixed delay: on fast machines, it updates almost instantly; on slow machines, it yields and catches up as soon as the main thread is idle.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The classic React 18 concurrency vs legacy debounce comparison.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Heavy Graph Chart Updates Driven by External Props
realWorldUseCases.description: Deferring chart redraws when receiving high-frequency telemetry updates from parent props.

howToExplain.opening: useDeferredValue defers re-rendering non-critical parts of the UI, lagging behind urgent updates without introducing artificial debounce delays.
keyPoints: Wraps values rather than state dispatchers.
Re-renders with previous value first, then schedules background render with new value.
Adapts dynamically to device CPU speed without fixed millisecond timers.
Can be checked via deferredValue !== value to show stale indicators.
howToExplain.closingImpression: useDeferredValue replaces arbitrary debounce timers with intelligent, CPU-aware deferred rendering.
analogies: A camera autofocus: the viewfinder shows the current view immediately, while the lens adjusts focus smoothly behind it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using useDeferredValue on a component that is not memoized.
commonMistakes.why: If the child component is not wrapped in React.memo, it will re-render anyway when the parent renders, defeating the deferred value bailout.
commonMistakes.correct: Pass deferredValue to a component wrapped in React.memo.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is the initialValue parameter in React 19 useDeferredValue?
followUpDeepDive.answer: React 19 added `useDeferredValue(value, initialValue)`: during initial render, it returns `initialValue` and schedules a deferred render with `value`, enabling clean progressive hydration.
